title: On Believing the oldest account in the book
subtitle: 价值观 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 价值观（做人与做事·价值观与人生意义）
meta: 主题语境：价值观（做人与做事·价值观与人生意义）　|　核心词汇：believe　|　正文 365 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 believe 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1982 the engineer ① believed the oldest account in the book without a word of thanks, and every worker in the workshop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the engineer ② believes the oldest account in the book at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ believe the oldest account in the book at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ believed the oldest account in the book before — a line in the manual for April 1976 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Believing the oldest account in the book without a word of thanks, the engineer said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the lever at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ believe the whole matter to be over at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Believe the whole matter to be over at once and never mention it again.

By 1989 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the manual, and a new worker from the next workshop ⑧ believes the whole matter to be over without a word of thanks every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ believed the oldest account in the book again when nobody else would.

⑩ To believe the oldest account in the book, my mother said in 1994, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the workshop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the workshop forgets, somebody believes the oldest account in the book at once again and somebody must believe the oldest account in the book without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 相信（一般过去式 believed the oldest account in the book：1982 年工程师头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 相信（一般现在 believes the oldest account in the book：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 相信（不定式 to believe the oldest account in the book：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 相信（过去完成时 had believed the oldest account in the book：1976 年四月的说明书上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 相信（动名词 believing the oldest account in the book 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 认为（believe the whole matter to be over：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去认为那件事已经过去了）
G. v. 认为（believe the whole matter to be over：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 相信（后段两处：新来的工人照例 believes the whole matter to be over，而母亲又一次 believed the oldest account in the book）

answers.why: believe 意为“相信”，1982 年工程师不图一句谢相信簿子里最老的那条记载，那是车间里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 believed。
believe 意为“相信”，自那以后工程师二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 believes。
believe 意为“相信”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯相信簿子里最老的那条记载”，此处为不定式 to believe the oldest account in the book。
believe 意为“相信”，说明书里 四月 那行字说明早在 1989 年之前就有人相信过，故用过去完成时 had believed。
believe 意为“相信”，工程师说“相信簿子里最老的那条记载这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 believing the oldest account in the book 作主语。
believe 意为“认为”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去认为那件事已经过去了”，should ever 之后用原形 believe the whole matter to be over。
believe 意为“认为”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻认为那件事已经过去了（believe the whole matter to be over at once），以后再也不要提起。
believe 意为“相信”，新来的工人每个年头都照例认为那件事已经过去了，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 believes。
believe 意为“相信”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢相信簿子里最老的那条记载，用一般过去式 believed 叙述。
believe 意为“相信”，结尾那句是母亲 1994 年的话：要相信簿子里最老的那条记载，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和车间记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 believe 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1982 the engineer believed the oldest account in the book without a word of thanks, and nobody in the workshop forgot it.
Even now the engineer believes the oldest account in the book at once whenever the workshop asks.
Believing the oldest account in the book without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever believe the whole matter to be over at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new worker from the next workshop believes the whole matter to be over without a word of thanks every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother believed the oldest account in the book again, and the workshop remembered that half.
